saints.name: St. Sylvester I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: The pope of the peace of the Church under Constantine, in whose reign Nicaea met and the great Roman basilicas rose…
biography: Sylvester, a Roman, son of Rufinus, became bishop of Rome in January 314 on the death of Miltiades, and governed the Church for twenty-one years. His pontificate spans the turning of the age: the Edict of Milan had just granted peace, and in his first year Constantine's council at Arles judged the Donatist schism.

In 325 the first ecumenical council assembled at Nicaea to condemn the teaching of Arius. The aged pope did not attend but sent as his legates the priests Vitus and Vincentius, while Hosius of Cordoba presided; the word homoousios was probably settled with him beforehand.

In his years rose Constantine's great Roman basilicas: the Lateran with its baptistery beside the palace where the pope dwelt, St. Peter's on the Vatican, the Sessorian church of the Holy Cross, and churches over the martyrs' graves; the first Roman martyrology, too, was likely drawn up under him.

Later legend made him the healer and baptizer of Constantine and the recipient of his 'Donation,' but these tales are apocryphal. He died on 31 December 335 and was buried in the church he had built over the catacomb of Priscilla on the Via Salaria; his feast closes the civil year.
saints.knownFor: Pope during the age of Constantine and the Council of Nicaea.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 31 December
